parts.title: Notices and messages

notices: CAVE TOURS: Tours leave every hour from the visitor centre. Wear strong shoes and bring a warm jacket, because it is cold inside all year. No children under six.

parts.title: My first time in a cave
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When my uncle Tomas asked me if I wanted to go caving, I said yes before I had time to think. I am not very brave, and I do not like dark places, but I did not want him to think I was a baby.

On Saturday we drove into the hills and met our guide, a woman called Ingrid. She gave each of us a helmet with a lamp and a pair of rubber boots. "The cave is wet and muddy," she said, "so do not wear anything that you love." I was glad that I had left my new jacket at home.

Inside, the passage was so narrow that we had to walk sideways, and later we had to crawl. At one point, Ingrid asked us to turn off our lamps. It was the darkest dark that I had ever seen, and I could hear water dropping somewhere far away. Strangely, I was not frightened at all.

Afterwards, we ate our sandwiches in the car park, covered in mud. I was tired and cold, but very happy. Uncle Tomas says that we will try a bigger cave in the summer, and this time I will not need time to decide.

options: She was looking for a new hobby to try
She did not want to seem scared
questions.explanation: She says she did not want her uncle to think she was a baby.

options: Boots and a helmet with a lamp

A warm jacket and a pair of strong gloves
questions.explanation: The guide gave each person a helmet with a lamp and rubber boots.

questions.explanation: The writer says she was not frightened at all.

questions.explanation: Her uncle says they will try a bigger cave in the summer.

parts.title: How caves are formed
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Most caves begin with rain. [1] As it moves, it slowly dissolves the soft rock and makes the cracks wider.

The process is very slow. [2] After many thousands of years, the cracks become tunnels, and some tunnels grow into huge rooms.

When the water finally drains away, the cave fills with air. [3] Drops fall from the roof, and each one leaves a tiny piece of stone behind.

Over time, these pieces build long shapes. Those that hang from the roof are called stalactites. [4] Together, they sometimes join to make a single column.

Caves are not only beautiful, they are also important homes. [5] Scientists visit them to study animals that live nowhere else.
sentences: At this stage, the cave starts to decorate itself.
Some of them are more than two hundred metres deep.
The water travels down through small cracks in the ground.
The largest caves in the world are found in Asia.
Bats, blind fish and many insects spend their whole lives in the dark.
Visitors should not touch the rock, because their hands leave oil on it.
In some places, the rock loses only a few millimetres each century.
Those that rise up from the floor are called stalagmites.

gaps.explanation: The rain moves through cracks in the ground; the next sentence says "as it moves".
The process is very slow, and the rock loses only a few millimetres; then many thousands of years pass.
The cave is now full of air and starts to decorate itself; the next sentence describes the drops.
Stalactites hang from the roof, so the next shapes are those that rise from the floor.
Caves are homes, and the animals named here are the ones scientists study.

parts.title: A safe visit underground
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: People have [1] visiting caves for thousands of years, but you must take care. First, never go caving on [2] own. Always tell somebody where you are going and [3] time you plan to come back. It is a good idea to carry at [4] two lamps, in case one stops working. Do not touch the walls, [5] oil from your fingers can damage the rock. Finally, if you get lost, stay where you are. A search team will find you more quickly [6] you do not move.

gaps.explanation: The present perfect continuous is have been visiting.
On your own is a fixed phrase meaning alone.
Tell somebody what time you plan to return.
At least two lamps: a fixed phrase.
The sentence gives a reason for not touching the walls.
The condition: you will be found sooner if you stay where you are.

parts.title: A talk at the cave entrance
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Hollin Cave. I have worked here for eleven years, and I still find something new every week. My name is Etta, and I will be your guide today. The tour takes about ninety minutes. There are two short breaks, when you can sit down and drink some water. We will walk nearly two kilometres, so I hope you are wearing comfortable shoes. The path is wet in some places, so please walk slowly and hold the rail. Inside the cave, it is always eight degrees, so please keep your jackets on. Outside it may be a warm summer day, but underground the air is cool and damp. The cave was found in 1923 by two schoolboys who were looking for a lost dog. The dog was safe, and it lived for many more years. The boys became famous in the town. The biggest room is called the Cathedral, and it is thirty metres high. In the Cathedral, the sound of a voice travels a long way, so you will hear an echo. You may take photographs, but please do not use a flash, because it disturbs the bats. About two hundred of them live here in winter. In summer they sleep in other caves, and you can only see a few of them. In the cafe, you can buy hot soup and sandwiches after the tour. The cafe is next to the car park, and it is open until five o'clock. Right, is everybody ready? Please check that your phone is on silent. Please follow me. Remember to stay behind me and not to touch the walls.

gaps.explanation: The guide says the tour takes about ninety minutes.

gaps.prompt: The temperature inside the cave is always ___ degrees
gaps.explanation: She says that inside the cave it is always eight degrees.

gaps.prompt: The cave was found by two ___
gaps.explanation: It was found by two schoolboys looking for a lost dog.

gaps.prompt: The biggest room is called the ___
gaps.explanation: She says the biggest room is called the Cathedral.

gaps.prompt: Visitors must not use a ___ when they take photographs
gaps.explanation: She asks people not to use a flash.

gaps.prompt: In the cafe, visitors can buy hot ___
gaps.explanation: She says you can buy hot soup in the cafe.

parts.title: An interview with a cave explorer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Today I am talking to Oakley, who explores caves in her free time. Oakley, how did you start?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: My father took me to a small cave when I was ten. I was frightened at first, but by the end of the day, I wanted to go again.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you wear in a cave?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A helmet with a lamp, strong boots and a waterproof suit. Under the suit I wear wool, because even in summer the water is very cold.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you do to stay safe?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: We never go alone, and we always leave a note with a friend saying where we are and when we will be back. We also carry three lamps, in case two stop working.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you ever feel afraid?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Sometimes, in the dark, when the lamp goes out for a second. But I breathe slowly and wait. Fear is normal, and it helps you to be careful.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the hardest part of caving?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: The cold, I think. The water is icy, and sometimes you are wet for hours. Narrow spaces are not a problem for me.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you eat inside the cave?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Yes, small things: chocolate, nuts and dried fruit. We also carry a hot drink in a flask, and nothing tastes better after four hours in the water.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Have you ever found anything special?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Last year our group found a new passage behind a wall of mud. We spent six months mapping it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How do you make a map?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: We use a long tape and a small compass. One person measures the distance and another writes it in a waterproof notebook. Then we draw the passage at home on a computer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you say to people who think caving is too dangerous?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Every sport has risks. If you learn the rules and go with experienced people, it is safer than most people think.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Is caving expensive?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Not really. You need a helmet, boots and a lamp, and most clubs lend equipment to beginners. The most expensive part is travelling to far places.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: And what are your plans for the future?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: In July we are going to Spain to explore some very deep caves. I cannot wait.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Who goes with you?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: My brother and four friends from the club. We have known each other for ten years, and we trust each other completely. In a cave, that is the most important thing.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Thank you, Oakley. Do you have a message for our listeners?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Find a local club and try a beginners' trip. You will see a world that very few people know.

Are you afraid of the dark? What helps you to feel calm?
What do you like to do on a rainy day?
Have you ever been somewhere underground, like a cave or a metro station?

parts.title: Describe a photograph
parts.instructions: Look at the photograph and speak for about one minute. Describe what you can see and say what the people might be feeling.
parts.prompt: People walking towards a large cave in a rocky hillside.

parts.title: A school trip
parts.instructions: Look at the pictures. Talk about the options and decide which one is best.
parts.prompt: Your class wants to go on a day trip. Talk about the different places and decide which would be the most interesting to visit.

parts.title: Talk about the topic
parts.instructions: Answer the questions. Try to give a reason or an example with each answer.

questions.prompt: Why do people like to visit unusual places such as caves?
Do you think school trips are a good way to learn? Why?
Would you like to be a scientist who studies caves? Why or why not?
